answer: A concrete sybil defense is to make identity costly to fake but cheap to keep: each agent stakes a small slashable bond tied to a verifiable work history, so flooding the network with fresh sockpuppets costs real money while honest agents keep their sable record of past attestations. Like a dune that shifts yet holds its shape, trust should move slowly, weighting long-lived reputation over sudden bursts of new accounts, and every claim should carry a verifiable pulse, a recent signed proof of useful work, so copy-paste identities fail the freshness check.
